name: Why do kitchen remodels in older Los Angeles homes uncover hidden problems?

mainEntity.name: Why do kitchen remodels in older Los Angeles homes uncover hidden problems?
mainEntity.text: Why do kitchen remodels in older Los Angeles homes uncover hidden problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older Los Angeles homes often reveal hidden problems during kitchen renovation because walls, floors, and cabinets can conceal decades of wear or past shortcut repairs. Common issues include outdated wiring, undersized electrical panels, old galvanized or corroded plumbing, uneven floors, structural modifications from prior remodels, and moisture damage around sinks or windows. In some homes, the original framing may not match modern layout plans, which means additional carpentry or leveling work is needed. These discoveries are one reason renovation budgets need contingency. Homeowners should expect the unexpected when opening walls in older properties, especially if the home has not been substantially updated. A contractor should inspect the kitchen carefully before demolition and explain which risks are likely based on the home’s age and condition. Building a contingency into the budget helps prevent project stress when hidden work appears.
acceptedAnswer.description: Older Los Angeles homes often hide outdated wiring, old plumbing, unlevel floors, damaged framing, or previous remodel shortcuts. These issues are usually invisible until demolition begins. Hidden conditions can increase cost and extend the schedule, especially when the kitchen has not been updated in decades.
